title: fix(git.commit.push): --auth as-human applies to the pr open, never to the push
description:
## .what

`git.commit.push --auth as-human` applies the human's gh login to the pr open only. the push itself (`git push origin HEAD --force-with-lease`, `git.commit.push.sh` line 496) runs with whatever credential helper the seat holds.

on a laptop whose https remote is served by a helper that declines (here a grove-only helper, `git-credential-keyrack`), the push falls through to a prompt and fails:

```
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git': No such device or address
```

so `--auth as-human` cannot push from a laptop seat, though its help and its own retry hint offer it as the escape from a keyrack failure.

## .why it matters

the documented fallback (`retry: rhx git.commit.push --mode apply --auth as-human`) is a dead end on the seat it is offered to. the caller is left with raw git config edits or a remote change.

## .the shape of the fix

under `as-human`, push through gh's own credential, scoped to the one command, so no global config changes:

```sh
git -c credential.helper= -c 'credential.helper=!gh auth git-credential' push origin HEAD --force-with-lease
```

strip ambient `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` the same way the pr open already does.

## .a second defect: three skills ship read-only, so no pnpm patch can touch them

`git.commit.push.sh`, `git.commit.set.sh`, and `keyrack.operations.sh` ship in 1.43.0 as mode `-r-xr-xr-x`; their peers ship `-rwxr-xr-x`. pnpm copies that mode into a patched dir. its applier then rewrites the file in place, the write throws on the read-only file, the error is swallowed, and pnpm reports only `ERR_PNPM_PATCH_FAILED` with no cause.

a consumer can work around it with `old mode 100644` / `new mode 100755` in the patch header. pnpm applies a mode change before the hunk, and it accepts only those two mode strings. the cure belongs at the source: publish all three as 0755, like their peers.

measured: uladkasach/dev-env-setup#213 carries that workaround and a clamp that is red without the patch and green with it.

clamp: a temp repo whose global helper declines; push under `as-human` to a local bare remote with a stub gh helper. red before the fix, green after.
